description: Reinforcement learning is a branch of machine learning focused on algorithmic decision-making. Its applications range from online platform advertisement to AlphaGo. The main objective of this course is to introduce fundamental concepts, theories, and algorithms for reinforcement learning. It covers the following topics: Bandit problems and algorithms, Markov decision problems, Bellman’s equation, epsilon-greedy algorithm, upper confidence bound method, temporal difference algorithms, Thompson sampling algorithm and policy gradient algorithms.
prerequisite: If undertaking an Undergraduate Degree THEN (( must have completed 1 of MA1505/MA1511/MA1521/MA2002 at a grade of at least D) AND ( must have completed 1 of MA3238/MA3270/ST3236 at a grade of at least D))
